entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-mv8x-fg99-32mf: hermes-agent has an Injection issue
entry.content:
hermes-agent has an Injection issue

Aliases: CVE-2026-10222, PYSEC-2026-2513

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P

Affected:

  • hermes-agent — fixed in 0.18.0

A security flaw has been discovered in NousResearch hermes-agent up to 2026.4.30. Affected by this issue is the function _sanitize_env_lines of the file hermes_cli/config.py. The manipulation results in injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The attack requires a high level of complexity. The exploitation is known to be difficult. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-2946: PraisonAI: Coarse-Grained Tool Approval Cache Bypasses Per-Invocation Consent for Shell Commands
entry.content:
PraisonAI: Coarse-Grained Tool Approval Cache Bypasses Per-Invocation Consent for Shell Commands

Aliases: CVE-2026-56074, GHSA-ffp3-3562-8cv3

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • praisonaiagents — fixed in 4.5.128

## Summary The approval system in PraisonAI Agents caches tool approval decisions by tool name only, not by invocation arguments. Once a user approves `execute_command` for any command (e.g., `ls -la`), all subsequent `execute_command` calls in that execution context bypass the approval prompt entirely. Combined with `os.environ.copy()` passing all process environment variables to subprocesses, this allows an LLM agent (potentially via prompt injection) to silently exfiltrate API keys and credentials without further user consent. ## Details The `require_approval` decorator in `src/praisonai-agents/praisonaiagents/approval/__init__.py:176-178` checks approval status by tool name only: ```python @wraps(func) def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): if is_already_approved(tool_name): # line 17…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-3fcr-jvgp-7f58: pytonapi has a Webhook Custom Path Authentication Bypass
entry.content:
pytonapi has a Webhook Custom Path Authentication Bypass

Aliases: CVE-2026-54635

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • pytonapi — fixed in 2.2.1

## Webhook Custom Path Authentication Bypass in pytonapi ### Summary `TonapiWebhookDispatcher` in pytonapi 2.2.0 fails to validate the `Authorization` header when a webhook handler is registered with the documented `path=` argument. During `setup()`, bearer tokens are stored only under the default suffix paths (e.g., `/hook/account-tx`), but the custom path (e.g., `/hook/custom`) is never added to the token map. When an incoming request arrives at the custom path, `self._tokens.get(path)` returns `None`, causing the `if expected_token is not None` guard to evaluate to `False` and silently skip authentication entirely. An unauthenticated remote attacker can POST arbitrary forged payloads to the custom webhook endpoint and trigger victim-defined handlers with full integrity impact. ### De…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-85rg-p3fr-xc2f: QTINeon has unauthenticated relay-to-host amplification via unbounded RECONNECT_REQUEST forwarding
entry.content:
QTINeon has unauthenticated relay-to-host amplification via unbounded RECONNECT_REQUEST forwarding

Aliases: CVE-2026-54609

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • com.quietterminal:qti-neon
  • qti-neon
  • qti-neon

### Impact The relay's reconnect handler forwards every `RECONNECT_REQUEST` to the host without deduplication or a size cap on the `pendingReconnects` map, unlike the connect flow which guards against this with `maxPendingConnections`. An unauthenticated attacker who knows a valid session ID can send `RECONNECT_REQUEST` packets from many spoofed source addresses; each packet that passes the session lookup is forwarded to the host as a new reconnect attempt. Because the per-source rate limiter assigns a fresh token bucket to each spoofed IP, it provides no protection. The host receives one forwarded packet per spoofed source per cleanup cycle, making the relay an amplification vector for denial-of-service against the host. The host's real address is never exposed to clients by design, so th…

entry.title: [UPDATED] PYSEC-2026-3492: OpenStack oslo.messaging does not verify RabbitMQ broker hostname during TLS handshake
entry.content:
OpenStack oslo.messaging does not verify RabbitMQ broker hostname during TLS handshake

Aliases: CVE-2026-44393, GHSA-76qh-xr7q-h39m

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • oslo-messaging

An issue was discovered in OpenStack oslo.messaging 1.0.0 through 17.3.0. The oslo.messaging RabbitMQ driver does not perform TLS hostname verification when connecting to the message broker. When ssl_ca_file is configured, the driver enables certificate chain validation but does not pass the expected broker hostname into the underlying TLS stack. Any certificate signed by the deployment CA is accepted regardless of hostname, allowing an attacker who can intercept control-plane traffic to impersonate the RabbitMQ broker and perform a man-in-the-middle attack on RPC and notification traffic. All OpenStack services using oslo.messaging with RabbitMQ over TLS are affected.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-434r-7c99-hwf3: Nanobot contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the web_fetch tool
entry.content:
Nanobot contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the web_fetch tool

Aliases: CVE-2026-49138

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:N/A:N · CVSS_V4: CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:L/SI:N/SA:N

Affected:

  • nanobot-ai — fixed in 0.2.1

Nanobot prior to version 0.2.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the web_fetch tool that allows remote attackers to reach internal or private network hosts by supplying a URL that redirects to a loopback or private address via a 3xx Location header. Attackers can exploit the automatic HTTP redirect following behavior in the httpx library to bypass initial URL validation and cause the runtime to send outbound requests to internal hosts before final resolved URL validation is applied.
